ai.summary: New .agents/base2/base2-max.ts and .agents/file-explorer/inline-file-explorer-max.ts define specialized agent variants. base2.ts refactored to export createBase2(mode) factory, conditionally including inline-file-explorer-max in spawnableAgents when mode is 'max'. toolNames updated to include 'spawn_agent_inline'. backend spawn-agent-inline.ts re-enables writeToClient streaming for inline agents, excluding context-pruner.

eli5.text: Today, when Buffy the Orchestrator runs a complex coding task, it can now choose a more powerful teamwork mode that lets it spawn an extra helper agent to read and explore code files more thoroughly, and that helper will stream its findings back live instead of hiding them. You would notice this only if you ran Buffy on the 'max' teamwork setting, where the helper it calls in for exploring files will now report its progress in real time so you can watch it work.

ai.title: Migrate evals to shallow git clones and add parentSha
ai.summary: Eval harness switched to shallow git clones. `parentSha` recorded per task. Files `evals/git-evals/*.json`, `gen-evals.ts`, `run-git-evals.ts`. Reduces clone size and enables precise commit tracking.

eli5.text: When you look at a past software project to check how a new feature performs, your tools now download only the essential history of that project instead of the entire record, which speeds things up and uses less storage. Each test run also now records the exact version of the code its results build on, so it's easier to trace back to the precise state later. This change is live today and affects only internal benchmarking, so you wouldn't notice it directly in your normal work.

ai.title: Refactor reviewer factory into reviewer.ts
ai.summary: Internal refactor. Moves `reviewerFactory` logic into `.agents/reviewer/reviewer.ts` as `createReviewer`. Deletes `.agents/reviewer/reviewer-factory.ts` and `.agents/reviewer/reviewer-max.ts`. Updates imports in `.agents/reviewer/reviewer-lite.ts` and `.agents/reviewer/reviewer.ts` to use the new local function.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the code that builds the code-reviewing assistant (the part that scans changes and flags issues) was reorganized: one definition file was removed and its building blocks were merged into another. Anyone who runs or maintains the reviewer tools will see a different file layout and one fewer configuration to update, but the review experience itself behaves the same. It is live as of this snapshot and has no effect beyond the internal reviewer setup.

ai.title: Editor agent preserves preexisting comments
ai.summary: The `editor` agent definition in `.agents/editor/editor.ts` updates the 'No code comments' rule. It now explicitly instructs the agent to keep preexisting comments, while still forbidding new ones unless requested. This clarifies behavior for edits touching commented code.

eli5.text: An internal assistant that helps write code is no longer deleting comments that were already in the file when it makes edits. Previously, the rule told it to never touch any comments, even ones that belonged to the code it was editing. Now it explicitly keeps those existing comments intact while still refusing to add new ones unless asked. If you looked at the assistant's instructions today, you'd see it now protects preexisting comments instead of stripping them out.

ai.title: Remove bun install initCommand from eval-codebuff2
ai.summary: Removed the `initCommand` field (value: `bun install`) from `evals/git-evals/eval-codebuff2.json`. This change aims to improve evaluation reliability and execution speed by eliminating the explicit dependency installation step during eval setup. The modification is internal to the Evals subsystem.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team removed the step that installed extra software tools before running a specific code test in the internal evaluation system. This test is part of how they check the assistant's coding performance, and it now starts up faster and runs more reliably without that extra installation step. If you looked, you would see the test configuration no longer includes a command that tells the system to download dependencies at startup. This only affects the internal evaluation process and does not change anything you experience directly.

ai.title: Add promptWithAgent flag to git evals
ai.summary: Introduced `promptWithAgent` boolean flag (default `false`) to control agent prompting behavior in git evals. Replaces internal `promptWithSpec` logic, altering `MAX_ATTEMPTS` and decision flow in `runSingleEval`. Propagated through CLI flags in `run-eval-set.ts` and process arguments in `run-single-eval-process.ts`.

eli5.text: When someone runs the evaluation tool from the command line, they can now choose whether the coding assistant tries multiple strategies to solve each task on its first attempt or gets a single, direct prompt to work with. If you opt into prompting with the agent, the system gives up after just one attempt instead of the usual five. This only affects the internal team running these evaluations behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add thinker-lite agent and refine base-lite prompts
ai.summary: Introduced `thinker-lite` agent using `x-ai/grok-4-fast` model. Updated `base-lite-grok-4-fast` to spawn `thinker-lite` instead of `thinker` and adjusted file reading instructions to target `file-explorer`/`find-all-referencer` agents with increased file count limits. Modified `base-lite` to use `gpt5-thinker` and `reviewer-lite` agents, removing `create_plan`, `add_subgoal`, and `update_subgoal` tools. Updated `base-prompts.ts` to conditionally exclude subgoal, background process, and plan creation instructions for lite agents.

eli5.text: If you use the lighter-weight version of this coding assistant, you'll now get access to a faster, simpler thinking helper that runs on a newer model, alongside a more streamlined review helper. The assistant will spawn these lighter helpers instead of the full versions, and it no longer sets up formal step-by-step plans before diving in. Behind the scenes, the instructions it follows were trimmed so the lighter mode doesn't include the background planning steps. These changes are live for internal use today.

ai.title: Inject promptAiSdk via DI in backend
ai.summary: Refactors backend LLM calls to accept `promptAiSdk` as a parameter instead of importing it directly. Updates functions in `admin`, `fast-rewrite`, `find-files`, and `generate-diffs` to use dependency injection for AI SDK interactions. This decouples core logic from the specific Vercel AI SDK implementation, improving testability and modularity.

eli5.text: Today, if you looked at the code, you'd see the parts that talk to external AI providers are now being told which provider to use instead of guessing that on their own. The backend still does the same thing, rewrite code, find files, run reviews, but each task now receives its AI helper as an explicit input, making it easier to swap providers or test changes without breaking the rest of the system. Nothing about what the tools actually do has changed yet; this is purely behind-the-scenes wiring for future flexibility.

ai.title: Rename WithDefaults to OptionalFields
ai.summary: Type alias `WithDefaults` renamed to `OptionalFields` across codebase. Update applies to `common/src/types/function-params.ts` and propagates to `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts`, `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts`, `packages/billing/src/org-billing.ts`, and `packages/internal/src/loops/client.ts`. Refactor improves semantic clarity for optional parameter definitions.

eli5.text: The system's internal code name for handling optional settings on functions was changed from 'WithDefaults' to 'OptionalFields' across the entire codebase. This is a behind-the-scenes naming update that developers use when writing new features and does not affect how anything works today, you won't notice any difference. It makes the code easier to understand for the engineers working on it.

ai.title: Disable getCustomFilePickerForOrg in requestRelevantFiles
ai.summary: Hardcoded `customFilePickerConfig` to `null` in `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts`, bypassing `getCustomFilePickerConfigForOrg`. The async call is commented out, and the null value is cast to the expected return type via `satisfies`. Scope limited to the file request prompt logic.

eli5.text: The system stopped looking up organization-specific file picker settings when gathering files to show you, so it now always uses the default selection instead of any customized one an organization may have set up. If you are in an organization that had a custom file picker configured, you no longer get that customized version during file requests. The old lookup code is still visible but commented out, meaning the custom behavior is effectively paused rather than removed. This is live today.

ai.title: Refactor auth to getUserInfoFromApiKey in AgentRuntimeDeps
ai.summary: Auth logic refactored to `getUserInfoFromApiKey` in `AgentRuntimeDeps`. Replaces `getUserIdFromAuthToken` and `getUserInfoFromAuthToken` with a generic, field-selectable API. Covers `backend/src/api/org.ts`, `usage.ts`, `websockets/auth.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `websocket-action.ts`, `impl/agent-runtime.ts`, and `common/src/testing/impl/agent-runtime.ts`. `getUserInfoFromApiKey` accepts `apiKey` and `fields` array, returning typed user subset or null.

eli5.text: The system's login check has been simplified so that one consistent method now verifies who you are across the app's main surfaces - the API, usage reporting, and real-time WebSocket connections. Instead of separate, hard-coded lookups for your account ID or profile details, there is now a single lookup that fetches exactly the pieces of your identity a given task needs (for example, just your unique ID or your email) and returns null when you cannot be identified. If you use the product today, you won't notice anything different, but the change means fewer scattered authentication helpers that each read your account table a slightly different way, which makes the auth surface easier to keep correct and extend. The refactor is live as of this build across the backend, websocket layer, and

ai.title: Expose CodebuffClientOptions types in SDK index
ai.summary: Added explicit type exports for CodebuffClientOptions and related tool interfaces to sdk/src/index.ts. Reordered existing type exports and included native ripgrep and tool helpers. Ensures SDK consumers have direct access to necessary client configuration types.

eli5.text: If you build something on top of the Codebuff assistant kit, you can now directly ask for the exact settings it takes to configure a client (like timeouts, tool lists, and connection options) instead of hunting through layers of types to find them. The team reordered and added a few of these building-block definitions to the main public listing so SDK users see everything they need in one place. This is live today, so anything built with the kit can reference these configuration types immediately. No behavior changed, it only clears the path so your code doesn’t have to guess what the client expects.

If you looked at the package's published list of exports today, you'd find that one item now points to a single source of truth. ai.title: Remove redundant tree-sitter query file existence test
ai.summary: Removed `testQueryFilesExist` from `sdk/test/tree-sitter-queries/test-query-files.js`. The check for file presence and validity is redundant because `bun` bundles these query files automatically. Only the functional tree-sitter test remains.

eli5.text: The developers removed an old self-check that repeatedly opened the file cabinet, counted every file, opened each one to make sure it wasn't empty, and confirmed each had the right ingredients before letting the main recipe proceed. That extra checking is now handled automatically when the program starts, so the test that did it by hand has been deleted, leaving only the test that actually proves the recipes still work. The house is cleaner and runs slightly faster, but you wouldn't see it change what the program does for you.

ai.title: Refactor agent validation and inject DB fetcher into runtime deps
ai.summary: Extracted `validateAgentNameHandlerHelper` to `backend/src/api/validate-agent-name.ts`, decoupling validation logic from `agents.ts`. Added `fetchAgentFromDatabase` to `BACKEND_AGENT_RUNTIME_IMPL` in `backend/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts`, enabling direct DB access within the agent runtime. Updated `main-prompt.ts` and `run-agent-step.ts` to pass expanded parameter types, allowing `getAgentTemplate` and `getAgentPrompt` to accept runtime dependencies directly. Moved `PROFIT_MARGIN` to `@codebuff/common/old-constants` in `message-cost-tracker.ts`.

eli5.text: The app's backend now checks agent names through a single, shared validation step instead of repeating that logic in multiple places, and the agent runtime can read an agent's stored profile directly from its database connection. Developers calling agent setup will notice their templates resolve using this new shared lookup, while end users can expect agent name validation to behave consistently across the service. This goes live today across the backend service, touching the agents and prompt-building layers.

ai.title: Replace checkAuthToken with getUserInfoFromApiKey in auth flow
ai.summary: Removed legacy `checkAuthToken` from `packages/internal/src/utils/auth.ts` and `backend/src/util/check-auth.ts`. Callers in `backend/src/api/usage.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts`, and `web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts` now use `getUserInfoFromApiKey`. This eliminates session-token DB joins in favor of API key validation. Admin checks and agent publishing rely on the new auth interface.

eli5.text: The service stopped verifying people through their web-browser session cookie and now requires every API request to come with a long-lived API key. If you use the usage dashboard, the WebSocket chat connection, or publish an agent, each call is checked against the key directly instead of by looking up a temporary session. The company removed the old session-based validation code, so any caller that still relies on session cookies without forwarding the API key will be rejected. This is already live today.

ai.title: Remove stray eval result file
ai.summary: Deleted `evals/git-evals/eval-result-codebuff-yyzy-SZKdI4.json` from the repository. This 65k-line artifact contained test specs and mock data for spawn-agent message history filtering, previously committed by mistake. Scope limited to the `evals` directory; no source code or configuration changes.

eli5.text: A large test-result file that had been accidentally saved into the project has been deleted, trimming the codebase by over 65,000 lines. This file was a leftover record of test specifications and mock data used for checking how child agents receive conversation history, so removing it only cleans up the repository without altering any live functionality. If you browsed the project's internal folder, you would no longer find this bulky JSON artifact sitting alongside the actual test files.

ai.title: Fix git-evals prompt turns and add date to logs
ai.summary: Corrected inverted logic for `promptWithAgent` in `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts`, ensuring proper `MAX_ATTEMPTS` and agent response handling. Eval logs now prefix filenames with ISO date strings for better traceability. Internal fix to eval runner stability and log organization.

eli5.text: When the automated assistant tried to figure out a coding task, it was using the wrong rule for how many times to try and whether to ask for help along the way, so it would either give up too soon or loop too long. That rule is now flipped to its correct setting, making these trial runs more stable and predictable for the team that builds and tests the assistant. You won't see these runs yourself, but the test records they leave behind now start with a date, so it's easier to find and sort them later.

ai.title: Multi-agent comparison for git evals
ai.summary: Added `run-eval-set-multi-agent.ts` to support parallel execution of multiple agents on the same eval tasks. The `run-eval-set` CLI now accepts a comma-separated `--agents` flag (e.g., `--agents base,base-lite,base2`) to trigger comparison mode, generating side-by-side metrics and comparison tables. This change affects the evals subsystem, specifically `evals/git-evals/run-eval-set.ts` and new types in `evals/git-evals/types.ts`.

eli5.text: If you run the test suite with a command like `--agents base,base-lite,base2`, the system now runs each of those helper versions on the same problems at the same time and then shows you a side-by-side scorecard so you can tell which version is best. Previously you could only ask about one helper at a time. The comparison report is generated automatically and saved alongside the regular test results. This only matters if you are the kind of person who launches these automated helper comparisons today.
